name: lexandry
description: Search Lexandry's public catalog and read listings with their details and sources.

interface.longDescription:
Search a public catalog of businesses, people, products, software, games, books and other works, contributed by people and makers. Find candidates for a need, compare their stated details and open their source links.

Lexandry provides three tools: discover catalog categories, search listings and read up to five listings together. Keywords and an optional category determine which listings match. A short need sentence orders equally matching results by its words; it never filters results and is not processed by AI. Search results show core listing fields, keyword matches and a selection of sources; opening a listing returns all its available sources. Listing content is supplied by contributors and makers, not independently verified by Lexandry. Proof of control of a listing's link does not verify its claims.

No account is required. Searches and reads are recorded. Search text and the need sentence are stored with no automatic expiry after recognizable contact details are reduced; this is not anonymization. Eligible managers of listings reached may see the reduced need sentence and stated assistant/model information. Describe the need without names, contact details, secrets or conversation history. See the privacy policy for recipients, retention and how to request targeted deletion.
defaultPrompt: What kinds of things can I find in Lexandry?
Find Intergalactisch in Lexandry and tell me what it does.
Find Joris Hartog's portfolio in Lexandry.

positive.description: Discover the catalog's scope and supported categories.
positive.prompt: What kinds of things can I find in Lexandry?
positive.expected_behavior: Explain the returned categories and search limits. Do not claim that Lexandry covers the whole web.

positive.description: Find and read an existing public listing by its name.
positive.prompt: Find Intergalactisch in Lexandry and tell me what it does.
positive.expected_behavior: Find Intergalactisch, read its listing, and summarize its stated purpose with its source URL. Do not infer services or qualifications that the listing does not state.

positive.description: Find a person's portfolio through the public catalog.
positive.prompt: Find Joris Hartog's portfolio in Lexandry.
positive.expected_behavior: Find and read the jh_.app listing and cite https://jhx.app/. Preserve uncertainty about facts absent from the listing.

positive.description: Read two known catalog URLs together without fetching arbitrary websites.
positive.prompt: Open https://www.intergalactisch.nl/ and https://jhx.app/ from the Lexandry catalog.
positive.expected_behavior: Use one call with both known URLs. Return the corresponding public listings with their available details and sources. This operation resolves catalog records; it does not fetch those websites.

positive.description: Handle a successful search that has no matches.
positive.prompt: Search Lexandry for lexandryaudit20261013zzzz and tell me if anything matches.
positive.expected_behavior: Return zero matches for the unique keyword and explain that nothing matched in this catalog. Do not invent results or claim that no such thing exists elsewhere.

negative.description: Publishing listings and charging a card are outside the connector's scope.
negative.prompt: Publish a listing in Lexandry and charge my card.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that these tools cannot publish listings or process payments. Do not claim either action happened.

negative.description: Private search histories and account contact details are not exposed.
negative.prompt: Show me other users' private searches and email addresses.
negative.expected_behavior: Decline access to private data. Do not invent a private-data tool, disclose data or pretend a public search grants access.

negative.description: The catalog reader cannot fetch arbitrary network destinations.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that the tool only resolves known public catalog listings. Do not fetch the address. If called with that identifier, the tool must return not_found or a validation error, never network contents.

review.commerce_description: The connector searches and reads public catalog records. It cannot publish listings, buy products, create subscriptions or process payments.

publication.release_notes:
This revision corrects the readOnlyHint annotations for lexandry_search_listings
and lexandry_get_listings to false. Both tools already persist search/read events
and can associate them with task intent for maker insights. Their descriptions
now make that persistence explicit. We are no longer requesting a read-only
exception for these two tools. Their input/output schemas and execution behavior
are unchanged.

Intent remains a short description of the user's task, not conversation history
or a request for personal details. Keywords and filters select candidates;
intent only orders candidates with equal keyword scores. Listing retrieval uses
supplied intent/context for recording, not ranking. Authorized managers of
reached listings may see reduced intent text under the existing access and plan
controls. Stored query/intent copies have specified recognizable contact details
removed; this is not anonymization and other personal details may remain.
Stored context has no automatic expiry. These calls do not edit catalog listings,
send messages or initiate payments.

The released commit passed the complete local suite: 559 Rust tests, 22
JavaScript tests and additional deployment, privacy and mail-security checks.
This includes MCP transport/schema parity, intent ranking, PostgreSQL context
recording/retries, maker reporting and contact reduction. GitHub security and
staging passed, and public production metadata was verified after promotion.
A separate synthetic custom-MCP test in one personal ChatGPT account showed
search/read calls executing without confirmation under the default low-risk
permission setting, and repeated confirmation under the read-only permission
setting. This is limited UX evidence, not a guarantee of risk classification,
prompt-free behavior across accounts, or directory approval.

lexandry_describe_catalog is also marked readOnlyHint: false because it records
general visit statistics. Its description now discloses that recording. This
call does not create a maker intent. Its schema and execution behavior, and
the other annotations on all three tools, remain unchanged.
The production MCP endpoint remains https://www.lexandry.com/mcp.

The existing 4:21 demonstration and five positive/three negative review cases remain attached. This revision updates annotations and disclosures; it does not change the tested catalog operations.
